newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, central bank ups fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, central bank ups fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the central bank had set a higher fixing as anticipated, triggering some dollar selling to the bank.
"I think the central bank might have absorbed some $500 million from the market this afternoon," one dealer said.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,330/2,522 and the conversion rate to 2,330/2,378.
One Japanese bank dealer said many operators had speculated the hike and had accumulated dollars at below the 2,330.0 level this morning.

"I think many people can laugh this afternoon. They have made some gains from the spread," he said. Local operators had lowered bids for dollars early in the day on anticipation of the move, so that they can sell it later to the central bank.
Offshore operators cannot sell dollars to Bank Indonesia.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,329.60/2,330.10 at 0850 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,329.80/30.00.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,328.70/29.15 and 2,328.30/28.80, respectively.
"It's a long queue to get to the central bank. People who had bought below 2,330 would like to square now," one said.
Dealers said swap rates had eased across the board after the fixing because operators were expecting ample liquidity on Thursday following dollar absorption by the central bank.
Overnight swap closed at 0.36/0.42. Tom/next swap edged down to 0.55/0.60 from 0.60/0.65 points.
One-month swap eased to 17.0/17.5 from 17.50/18.25, two to 33.0/34.0 from 33.0/34.5, three to 50.5/51.5 from 52.0/52.5 and six to 97.0/98.0 from 99.0/100.0 points.
